/-!
# Big-line-big-clique conjecture

The big-line-big-clique conjecture of Kára, Pór and Wood (2005) states that every
sufficiently large finite set of points in the Euclidean plane contains either many
collinear points (a "big line") or many mutually visible points (a "big clique" in the
visibility graph).

Two distinct points $p, q$ of a point set $P$ are *visible* with respect to $P$ if no point
of $P$ lies in the open line segment between $p$ and $q$. In Lean this is `IsVisible ℝ P p q`.

The conjecture is only stated for finite point sets: Pór and Wood showed that it fails for
infinite point sets (there is a countably infinite planar point set with no $4$ collinear
points and no $3$ pairwise visible points).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big-line-big-clique_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KPW05] Kára, Jan; Pór, Attila; Wood, David R., *On the chromatic number of the visibility
  graph of a set of points in the plane*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 34 (2005), 497–506.
- [PW10] Pór, Attila; Wood, David R., *The big-line-big-clique conjecture is false for infinite
  point sets*. [arXiv:1008.2988](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2988)
-/

blocks.docstring:
**Big-line-big-clique conjecture** (Kára, Pór, Wood [KPW05]).

For all integers $k \geq 2$ and $\ell \geq 2$ there is an integer $n$ such that every finite set
$P$ of at least $n$ points in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains
* $\ell$ collinear points (a "big line"), or
* $k$ pairwise visible points (a "big clique"),

where two distinct points $p, q \in P$ are *visible* with respect to $P$ if no point of $P$ lies
in the open line segment between $p$ and $q$.

The cases $k \leq 1$ or $\ell \leq 1$ are trivial, so this is equivalent to the version for all
positive integers $k, \ell$. The conjecture is known to hold for $k \leq 5$ or $\ell \leq 3$, and
is open for $k = 6$ or $\ell = 4$.

claims.decomposer_note: Kára–Pór–Wood (2005): for all integers k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2 there exists n such that every FINITE set of at least n points in ℝ² contains ℓ collinear points or k pairwise visible points, where distinct p, q are visible w.r.t. P iff no point of P lies in the open segment (p,q); the point set must be finite (the infinitary version is false, Pór–Wood), 'mutually visible' means k distinct points of P pairwise visible, the quantifier is 'at least n points' per the primary sources (Wikipedia's 'every set of n points' is a loose paraphrase, and visibility is not monotone under taking subsets), and Wikipedia's 'positive integers k, ℓ' vs the sources' k, ℓ ≥ 2 makes no difference since the k = 1 or ℓ = 1 cases are trivial.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematical content, matching the Kára–Pór–Wood conjecture as quoted verbatim in Pór–Wood (arXiv:1008.2988): ∀ k ℓ ≥ 2, ∃ n, every Finset P ⊆ ℝ² with n ≤ P.card has an ℓ-subset that is Collinear ℝ or a k-subset that is Set.Pairwise visible w.r.t. P. c07 was chosen as the base because (a) it uses Mathlib's existing `IsVisible ℝ (P : Set ℝ²)` instead of a bespoke `Visible` (c01/c05/c06) or an inline openSegment formula (c02/c08), as AGENTS.md prefers; (b) it uses `Finset ℝ²` rather than `Set ℝ² + P.Finite + ncard` (c02/c03), which is simpler and avoids ncard default-value concerns; (c) it has the most complete docstring and references. I verified in a scratch proof that for p ≠ q, `IsVisible ℝ P p q ↔ ∀ r ∈ P, r ∉ openSegment ℝ p q` (via sbtw_iff_mem_image_Ioo_and_ne and openSegment_eq_image_lineMap), and `Set.Pairwise` only ranges over distinct pairs, so the `IsVisible.rfl` convention for p = q is never consulted. Edits to c07: copyright year 2026, `open scoped EuclideanGeometry`, capitalised Wikipedia URL, and a docstring sentence noting equivalence with Wikipedia's 'positive integers k, ℓ'. Finiteness (Finset), 'at least n' (n ≤ P.card), distinctness (Finset card), visibility relative to the whole ambient set P, and quantifier order ∀k∀ℓ∃n∀P are all faithful. Boundary cases: n may be 0 (harmless under ∃); k, ℓ ≥ 2 hypotheses are satisfiable; no vacuous implications.

P, k, ℓ ≥ 2) agree with the primary literature (Pór–Wood arXiv:1008.2988, Abel et al. arXiv:0904.0262, Ghosh–Goswami arXiv:1012.5187) and were followed.

namespace BigLineBigCliqueConjecture

/--
**Big-line-big-clique conjecture** (Kára, Pór, Wood [KPW05]).

For all integers $k \geq 2$ and $\ell \geq 2$ there is an integer $n$ such that every finite set
$P$ of at least $n$ points in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains
* $\ell$ collinear points (a "big line"), or
* $k$ pairwise visible points (a "big clique"),

where two distinct points $p, q \in P$ are *visible* with respect to $P$ if no point of $P$ lies
in the open line segment between $p$ and $q$.

The cases $k \leq 1$ or $\ell \leq 1$ are trivial, so this is equivalent to the version for all
positive integers $k, \ell$. The conjecture is known to hold for $k \leq 5$ or $\ell \leq 3$, and
is open for $k = 6$ or $\ell = 4$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem big_line_big_clique_conjecture (k ℓ : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hℓ : 2 ≤ ℓ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset ℝ², n ≤ P.card →
      (∃ L ⊆ P, L.card = ℓ ∧ Collinear ℝ (L : Set ℝ²)) ∨
      (∃ Q ⊆ P, Q.card = k ∧ (Q : Set ℝ²).Pairwise (IsVisible ℝ (P : Set ℝ²))) := by
  sorry

end BigLineBigCliqueConjecture

items: The plane is `ℝ²` = `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (the repository's scoped notation from FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Geometry.2d), and point sets are `Finset ℝ²`, enforcing the finiteness required by the primary sources (the infinitary version is false, Pór–Wood).

The size hypothesis is `n ≤ P.card` ('at least n points'), following the primary sources rather than Wikipedia's 'every set of n points'; visibility is not monotone under taking subsets so this choice matters.

Visibility is Mathlib's `IsVisible ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) p q` (no point of P is Sbtw p _ q). For distinct p ≠ q this is exactly 'no point of P lies in the open segment (p,q)'; for p = q it is trivially true, but the clique condition is `Set.Pairwise`, which only ranges over distinct pairs, so this convention has no effect. Visibility is taken with respect to the whole set P (any point of P may block), not just the clique Q.

'ℓ collinear points' is a sub-Finset L ⊆ P with L.card = ℓ and `Collinear ℝ (L : Set ℝ²)`; 'k mutually visible points' is a sub-Finset Q ⊆ P with Q.card = k and pairwise visibility. Finset cardinality enforces distinctness of the points.

Parameters are restricted to k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, following Kára–Pór–Wood / Pór–Wood / Ghosh–Goswami, rather than Wikipedia's 'positive integers'. The excluded cases k ≤ 1 or ℓ ≤ 1 are trivially true (a single point is a 1-clique / 1 point is collinear), so the two formulations are equivalent.
AMS tags 5 (combinatorics) and 52 (convex and discrete geometry) were chosen; category is `research open` (open for k = 6 or ℓ = 4).

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; every candidate formalized it and none omitted. The Wikipedia list entry is a one-line description, so the precise statement was taken from the primary source (Pór–Wood's quotation of KPW05), as the decomposition notes prescribe: finite point sets only (infinite version is false), 'at least n points' rather than 'exactly n' (visibility is not monotone under subsets), k, ℓ ≥ 2 (k = 1 or ℓ = 1 trivially true, so equivalent to Wikipedia's 'positive integers'). Candidates c05/c06 also included extra 'variants' declarations (known cases k ≤ 5, ℓ ≤ 3; Pór–Wood infinite counterexample); these are not slots under adjudication and were not shipped, per the instruction to include exactly the surviving slots. All candidate files compiled; the final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning. The one line over 100 characters is a URL, which the linter exempts and which is common in the Wikipedia directory.
